name: Button
description: Primary action trigger used for form submissions, CTAs, and key interactions. Available in multiple visual variants and sizes.

label.description: Visible text label for the button

accessibility.aria_label: Not needed if visible label exists; required for icon-only buttons

do: Use filled variant for primary actions (one per section)
Use outlined for secondary actions alongside a primary button
Use ghost for low-emphasis tertiary actions
Use danger variant only for destructive actions like delete
Always include a visible text label
Place primary action on the right in button groups
dont: Don't use more than one filled button per section
Don't use Button for navigation — use a link instead
Don't disable without explaining why
Don't use danger variant for non-destructive actions
Don't put too much text in the label — keep it to 1-3 words

name: IconButton
description: Compact button for icon-only actions. Always requires an accessible label since there is no visible text.

aria-label.description: Accessible label (required since no visible text)

accessibility.aria_label: REQUIRED — must describe the action (e.g., 'Delete item', 'Open settings')

do: Always provide aria-label describing the action
Use ghost variant for toolbar and header actions
Use a tooltip to show the label on hover
Ensure the icon clearly communicates the action
dont: Never omit aria-label — this is an accessibility violation
Don't use for primary actions — use Button with visible text instead
Don't use ambiguous icons without a tooltip
Don't make icon buttons smaller than 44x44px touch target

name: Alert
description: Persistent inline message for important information. Stays visible until dismissed by the user. Use for contextual feedback within a page section.

severity.description: Visual severity level that sets color and icon

accessibility.role: role=alert for error/warning; role=status for info/success
accessibility.contrast_ratio: 4.5:1 for alert text against alert background
accessibility.focus_indicator: Dismiss button has visible focus ring
accessibility.keyboard: Dismiss button focusable and activatable via Enter/Space

do: Always include an icon — never rely on color alone (WCAG 1.4.1)
Use error for blocking issues that must be resolved
Use warning for potential issues the user should know about
Use info for helpful context or tips
Use success for confirming completed actions
Place alerts near the content they relate to
dont: Don't use Alert for transient feedback — use Toast instead
Don't use more than 2 alerts on a single view
Don't use error severity for non-blocking information
Don't auto-dismiss alerts — they should persist until addressed

name: Badge
description: Small label for showing status, counts, or categories. Can appear as a dot, a number, or a text label.

label.description: Text content (for label and count variants)

accessibility.aria_label: Provide aria-label for dot variants (no visible text)

do: Use dot variant for simple presence indicators
Use count variant for notification counts
Use label variant for status text (e.g., 'New', 'Beta')
Position badges relative to their parent element
Include text alternative for dot-only badges
dont: Don't use badges for interactive actions — they are read-only
Don't rely on color alone to convey meaning
Don't use long text in badges — keep to 1-2 words

name: Input
description: Text input field for capturing user data in forms. Supports validation states, helper text, and prefix/suffix elements.

label.description: Visible label text above the input

errorMessage.description: Error message shown in error state

prefix.description: Element before input text (icon or text)

suffix.description: Element after input text (icon or text)

accessibility.aria_label: Use visible label via <label> element (preferred) or aria-label
accessibility.keyboard: Tab to focus, type to input, Enter to submit in forms

do: Always include a visible label above the input
Use helper text to explain expected format
Show specific error messages (not just 'Invalid')
Use aria-describedby to link helper/error text to input
Mark required fields with aria-required and visual indicator
dont: Don't use placeholder as a replacement for labels
Don't use red color alone for errors — include an error message
Don't disable inputs without explaining why
Don't auto-clear input on error — let users correct their entry

name: Checkbox
description: Toggle control for boolean options or multi-select lists. Supports checked, unchecked, and indeterminate states.

label.description: Visible label text beside the checkbox

indeterminate.description: Shows a dash, used for partial selection in groups

accessibility.aria_label: Use visible label linked via <label> element
accessibility.keyboard: Space to toggle, Tab to navigate between checkboxes

do: Always include a visible label beside the checkbox
Group related checkboxes with a fieldset and legend
Use indeterminate state for parent checkbox of a partially selected group
Allow users to click the label (not just the checkbox) to toggle
dont: Don't use a checkbox for binary on/off settings — use a Toggle/Switch instead
Don't use a single checkbox for agreeing to terms without a visible label
Don't nest checkbox groups more than one level deep

name: Select
description: Dropdown control for choosing one option from a list. Opens a popover menu of options on click.

label.description: Visible label text above the select

placeholder.description: Placeholder shown when no option is selected

errorMessage.description: Error message shown in error state

accessibility.keyboard: Enter/Space to open, Arrow keys to navigate, Enter to select, Escape to close

do: Always include a visible label above the select
Use placeholder text to hint at expected selection
Provide a clear list of 3-15 options (use autocomplete for longer lists)
Show the selected option clearly in the trigger
dont: Don't use Select for binary choices — use Checkbox or Toggle
Don't use Select for fewer than 3 options — use Radio buttons
Don't use Select for very long lists (50+) — use an autocomplete/combobox
Don't auto-submit on selection change without warning

name: Toast
description: Auto-dismissing notification for transient, non-critical feedback. Appears briefly and disappears automatically. Use for confirmations and minor updates.

accessibility.contrast_ratio: 4.5:1 for toast text against dark background
accessibility.keyboard: Tab to focus action button, Escape to dismiss

do: Use for confirming successful actions (e.g., 'Changes saved')
Keep messages short — 1 sentence maximum
Set appropriate duration (3-8 seconds depending on text length)
Allow manual dismissal even with auto-dismiss
Stack multiple toasts if needed (newest on top)
dont: NEVER use Toast for errors or critical information — use Alert instead
Don't use Toast for information that needs to persist
Don't use warning or error severity with Toast
Don't require user action via Toast — it may auto-dismiss before they see it
Don't show more than 3 toasts simultaneously
